name: Richardson House
use: Former mini-dorm (43 students), mostly singles; First Year Experience; part of the four-building Minis
style: Two-storey wood-frame houses with vertical board siding and gabled roofs (from photos)
statusNote: Minis closed at the end of spring 2026; future not announced

facts.text: Dedicated October 17, 1976 as a residence for students interested in outdoor recreation, named for zoology professor Edythe T. Richardson; it later became home to the First Year Experience.

Housing's Minis pages (archived April 2026) state the Minis were expected to close permanently at the end of the spring 2026 semester and were not available for 2026-27 assignments; the live pages now return "Access denied" and the Minis are absent from the current residence-hall list.

Housing described Richardson (43 students) as a small community built around single rooms, with two lounges. The four Minis (Eaton, Hall, Marston, Richardson) functioned as one hall; residents could swipe into all four.
Accessibility per Housing: limited-use bathrooms, roll-in building access, strobe alerts in some rooms; gender-inclusive restrooms. No elevator or AC listed.

verdict: The smallest of the 1976 board-clad Minis, a homey first-year option until it closed in 2026.
notes: Reference photos show the Minis as low two-storey wood-frame buildings clad in grey vertical boards, with gabled roofs, exterior stairs and decks, set among tall pines near College Woods; modest, cabin-like, weathered. Lounge photo: sloped ceiling, carpet, a band of windows and a glazed door to a deck; plain finishes, decent daylight. No licensed photo found.
judgeNotes: Reference photos show a weathered cabin and a plain lounge. Down about a point from the old run because the Minis closed in 2026 (condition and function 3).
